artifacts.summary: All 5 plan phases completed: --consumer-report flag added to deploy-headless.sh (default OFF), test-deploy-verify-wiring.sh regression cases added, runtime confirmation of both modes, and doc updates.

completion_data.completion_summary: Gated deploy-headless.sh's post-deploy ~50-repo consumer-freshness walk behind a new default-OFF --consumer-report flag, removing it from the /orchestrate inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint's blocking path while preserving byte-compatible CONSUMERS_STALE=<n> output and exit-code neutrality when the flag is passed. Added 4 regression cases to test-deploy-verify-wiring.sh (20/20 passing) and updated 2 prose docs describing the scan's behavior.

memory_candidates.content: When a fixture-driven test suite resolves the script under test via find_script() preferring the deployed .claude/ tree over the source store (a common pattern in this repo's tests/*.sh suites), a source-store edit will NOT be visible to the tests until an intermediate `deploy-headless.sh` (default, non-wipe) redeploy syncs it. Run that redeploy before the regression-case phase, not after — it doubles as an early runtime-confirmation step rather than being wasted work.

verify-deploy.sh's full (non---skip-slow) gate set includes gate 8, the shell test suite runner (tests/run-all.sh), which runs the entire suite across the codebase and can take 10+ minutes wall clock. When time-bounded, the --skip-slow tier (which deploy-headless.sh's own inline verification already exercises on every deploy) is a much faster and still-meaningful confirmation that a change has not regressed the fast gate set; reserve the full non---skip-slow run for cases where the extra minutes are budgeted.
